source_evidence: Unlike other life insurance, variable life insurance has a cash value that varies depending, in part, on the performance of investments you choose from a menu of investment options—typically mutual funds.
answer: Variable life insurance combines life insurance with an investment-linked cash value. It pays a death benefit to beneficiaries, while the policy’s cash value can rise or fall based partly on the investment options you select. Because those investments can perform poorly and policy fees and expenses reduce account value, the policy can lose money and may lapse if its cash value is not sufficient to cover charges. Policy details, investment choices, and costs differ, so understand the specific policy before considering it.
